verses.1: For the leader; according to "The Lily of...." A miktam of David (for teaching),
verses.2: when he fought against Aram-Naharaim and Aram-Zobah; and Joab, coming back, killed twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
verses.3: O God, you rejected us, broke our defenses; you were angry but now revive us.
verses.4: You rocked the earth, split it open; repair the cracks for it totters.
verses.5: You made your people go through hardship, made us stagger from the wine you gave us.
verses.6: Raise up a flag for those who revere you, a refuge for them out of bow shot. Selah
verses.7: Help with your right hand and answer us that your loved ones may escape.
verses.8: In the sanctuary God promised: "I will exult, will apportion Shechem; the valley of Succoth I will measure out.
verses.9: Gilead is mine, mine is Manasseh; Ephraim is the helmet for my head, Judah, my own scepter.
verses.10: Moab is my washbowl; upon Edom I cast my sandal. I will triumph over Philistia."
verses.11: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me into Edom?
verses.12: Was it not you who rejected us, God? Do you no longer march with our armies?
verses.13: Give us aid against the foe; worthless is human help.
verses.14: We will triumph with the help of God, who will trample down our foes.

notes.text: These verses occur again as the second half of Psalm 108.
I will apportion... measure out: God lays claim to these places. The valley of Succoth: probably the lower stretch of the Jabbok valley.
Judah, my own scepter: an allusion to the Testament of Jacob, Genesis 49:10.
Moab is my washbowl: Moab borders the Dead Sea, hence a metaphor for the country. Upon Edom I cast my sandal: an ancient legal gesture of taking possession of land.
The fortified city: perhaps Bozrah, the fortified capital of Edom. Cf Isaiah 34:6; 63:1; Amos 1:12.
